turns.user: Compare the free tiers of Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare Pages for a small side project.
turns.answer:
All three are free for a side project, but they limit you differently. As of 11 Nov 2026:

| | Vercel Hobby | Netlify Free | Cloudflare Pages Free |
|---|---|---|---|
| Usage cap | 100 GB data transfer and 1M function invocations | 300 credits/month | Unlimited requests on static projects |
| Builds | 100 deployments/day | 15 credits per production deploy; previews free | 500 builds/month, 1 at a time |
| If you exceed it | Wait 30 days to use the feature again | All projects on your account pause | Not covered in my results |
| Catch | Non-commercial use only | Hard limit, no overage charges | 25 MiB max file size |

- **Vercel:** The cap is easy to hit with functions. Cron jobs can only run once per day.
- **Netlify:** Credits cover bandwidth, requests and compute together, so 300 can run out faster than the old fixed limits. One example is 20 credits per GB of bandwidth.
- **Cloudflare:** It's the most generous for static sites. Adding Functions changes that, because every request then invokes your Function by default.

For a static or mostly static side project, Cloudflare Pages is the safest free option. If you need server-side features, Vercel is the better fit as long as the project stays non-commercial.
